content: test modules in this project allow clippy::unwrap_used / indexing_slicing / expect_used / panic via #[allow(...)] on the test mod, since the project's clippy config denies these globally but tests need direct indexing and unwrap for clarity

name: wave-1-deadcode-allow
description: Wave 1 scaffolds for binary crates where most pub items are reached only by tests need a crate-level #![allow(dead_code)] in main.rs. The Wave 2/3 modules will exercise these symbols; without the allow, dev builds emit 36+ dead_code warnings that fail the zero-warnings acceptance gate

title: single-pass validation accumulator surfaces every S/G/F/W/T violation per validate() call
rationale: Operators with N typos shouldn't have to restart the validator N times. validate() returns Result<(), Vec<ValidationError>>; parse-time errors (curve structural rules) still short-circuit because by the time a curve fails to construct, downstream rules cannot meaningfully run. Two-tier failure model: parse errors stop early, validation errors accumulate. PLAN.md §Configuration Validation explicitly mandates accumulation behavior

name: cherry-pick-validate-foundation
description: When a sibling agent has produced a Wave-1 foundation commit (build setup + pure modules + I/O stubs) on a branch, prefer 'git cherry-pick <sha>' onto your worktree branch over rebuilding from scratch. After cherry-pick, run the full quality gate suite (cargo build dev+release, fmt --check, clippy -D warnings, cargo test) and audit the diff against the spec acceptance criteria (test name coverage for each validation rule, no I/O imports in pure modules, exact lint block, panic=abort). Lossless and produces an identical 14-file Wave-1 tree in seconds.

name: watchdog-disabled-state-pattern
description: HardwareWatchdog uses an internal enum WatchdogState { Enabled { file, accepted_timeout_s }, Disabled } so feed/disarm_and_close become trivial no-ops when [watchdog].enabled=false. Keeps the main daemon loop branch-free (no Option<HardwareWatchdog>); same calls work either way. Pairs cleanly with disarm_and_close consuming self.

content: Use nix::libc::c_int (re-exported by nix) for ioctl payload types instead of declaring libc as a direct dependency. This crate's only direct dep with libc is nix; calling out libc::c_int explicitly would require adding libc to Cargo.toml. nix::ioctl_readwrite!(name, b'W', 6, nix::libc::c_int) compiles cleanly without that addition.

name: snapshot-and-restore-pwm-enable
description: I/O modules that flip a sysfs control register (pwm_enable etc) must snapshot the kernel's exact bytes (after trim) before mutating, and round-trip those bytes verbatim on restore. Hard-coding a 'sane default' like '2' silently breaks chips whose semantics differ (Nuvoton's pwm_enable=2 = thermal cruise, not 'BIOS auto'). Test canary: use a non-trivial snapshot value like '5' so an implementer who 'fixes the test' to match a hard-coded restore value gets caught immediately.

content: I/O modules use std::fs directly + a tempfile-backed test directory that mimics sysfs layout (pwm{N}, pwm{N}_enable, fan{N}_input). No traits introduced (ADR-0006). Tests construct a fake hwmon dir via a make_hwmon_with_channel(dir, n, pwm_enable) helper and point the struct's hwmon_path at dir.path().

description: thiserror auto-applies #[source] to any field literally named 'source'; if its type doesn't impl std::error::Error (e.g. String), compilation fails with cryptic AsDynError trait-bound error
resolution: rename the field (e.g. 'cause'). Keep 'source' only when the value is a real error type like std::io::Error

name: fakenvml-cell-counter
description: TempReader trait takes &self, so FakeNvml's fail_after counter uses Cell<u32> for interior mutability. Both NvmlReader and FakeNvml route through one shared check_bounds() helper so the [5,110] contract has a single source of truth — required because FakeNvml stores Celsius (i16) while NvmlReader gets u32 from the wrapper

content: scan_at(&Path) is NOT #[cfg(test)]-gated — it's the public testable surface that production scan() wraps with the /sys/class/hwmon root. Same lesson applies to any future I/O module: the testable form IS the public API (PLAN.md L757).

name: daemon-defer-slam-after-mut-borrow
description: Inside the per-fan loop where we hold fans.get_mut(fan_id), we cannot also call slam_all_fans_to_max(&mut fans) when fault_tracker.tick_fan returns a fault — borrowck rejects two mutable borrows. Defer with a should_slam bool collected during the inner loop and call slam_all_fans_to_max(&mut fans, &mut spin_up_entries) once after the per-group iteration completes. Watchdog feed gating still kicks in immediately because it reads fault_tracker.any_fault(); the slam is best-effort override-to-max.

content: Smoke tests run env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_<name>") with config paths anchored to env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR") joined with the relative repo path; this works regardless of cargo's invocation cwd and does not require a separate build step (cargo test builds the binary automatically and exposes its path via CARGO_BIN_EXE).

name: daemon-init-shutdown-anyhow-no-expect
description: main.rs daemon composition root uses anyhow::Result + Context throughout init so every failure path returns cleanly via ? without invoking expect() — keeps cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings happy under the project-wide expect_used = 'warn' lint. Pattern: convert each module-specific error (LoggerError, ChipError, NvmlError, WatchdogError, FanError) via .context()/.with_context() at the call site. Init still respects ADR-0003 ordering — early returns leave fans under BIOS control because the watchdog isn't armed yet.

Cargo.toml's release_max_level_info plus -D warnings clippy gate work together such that any pub enum variant in production code that's never constructed (e.g. LoggerError::Journald, declared for a strict-journald path that the current logger doesn't use) will fail the gate once Wave 1's crate-wide #![allow(dead_code)] is removed in Wave 3.
resolution: Either remove the variant or annotate it with a focused #[allow(dead_code)] and a comment explaining why it's reserved. Crate-wide allow restoration is forbidden by spec.

description: rust-ini 0.21 includes inline '# ...' / '; ...' comments in the value unless the 'inline-comment' cargo feature is enabled. Default ParseOption has no enabled_inline_comment flag in 0.21.x. A verbatim INI with 'config_version = 1   # explanation' produces 'expected u32: invalid digit found in string' because the parser hands '1   # explanation' to .parse::<u32>().
resolution: Set rust-ini = { version = "0.21", features = ["inline-comment"] } in Cargo.toml. No src/ change required.
